transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Priya (KiteWave), Ethan (KiteWave SRE), Marisol (KiteWave Product), Tom (KiteWave Infra)

[00:00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — agenda is safety checks for deployment, confirm A/B cutover plan, monitoring knobs, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:12] Priya: Yep, that's what we want. We have the exec alignment for next week so this is the last POC sync before staging dry-run.
[00:00:25] Daniel: Cool. I'll run through current telemetry, recent perf numbers, and the proposed canary ramp with thresholds.
[00:00:33] Ethan: Before you start, real quick — we saw a spike in tail latency on Friday when prefix cache was cold, wanted to see if that's reproduced on Redwood dedicated or if it's our end.
[00:00:45] Daniel: Right, that was the KV cache warm-up issue — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — it's basically prefix and kv-cache fill. On Dedicated we see similar behavior if the prefix set is very diverse; our suggestion was a short pre-warm step in the runbook.
[00:01:02] Tom: Pre-warm how? Do we pre-send a sample of warmup prompts or run a synthetic batch?
[00:01:09] Daniel: Synthetic batch — we recommend a small set of representative prompts at low QPS for 10 minutes. We'll provide a script. That reduces p99 by about 40% in our test.
[00:01:22] Marisol: And that script lives in the runbook you mentioned?
[00:01:25] Sofia: Exactly. I'll share the runbook after the call. It's the cutover playbook plus rollback checklist.

[00:02:10] Daniel: Ok, I'll pull up the telemetry snapshot. Note — transcription may say Redwood API as 'Red wood a p i' — little audio artifact — but the metrics are: steady-state QPS 180, median latency 23 ms, p95 110 ms, p99 340 ms during the last 48 hours on the pilot. The spike Ethan mentioned aligns with a cache miss pattern.
[00:02:35] Ethan: The 340ms p99 is a concern for product folks; our internal SLO is 200ms p99. Is A/B able to route only a portion so we don't breach that across the whole fleet?
[00:02:49] Sofia: Yes — A/B routing allows you to send, say, 15% to the new variant and 85% to control. Canary ramp then increments at defined gates. We propose starting at 5%, hold 30 minutes, check metrics, then 20%, hold, etc.
[00:03:04] Priya: We had chatted internally about faster ramps — exec wants to see feature usage quickly. Can we do a faster ramp if metrics look stable?
[00:03:12] Daniel: You can, but you need automated guards. Our suggested gates: p50, p95, p99, error rate, and a quality proxy (we can use a rerank score or a small eval set). If any gate trips beyond threshold, automatic rollback to control.
[00:03:27] Marisol: What's the quality proxy you mentioned?
[00:03:30] Daniel: We recommend a lightweight regression test set — about 50 prompts representing your top intents — run every 5 minutes during canary. If the semantic similarity or confidence drops, that's a red flag. We'll include the harness in the gates.

[00:04:10] Tom: On infra — what's the recommended canary traffic percentage? Are we starting at 1%, 5%, 10%?
[00:04:15] Daniel: For model variant changes with potential latency differences, start at 5%. For config-only changes maybe 10%. For you, given the p99 concern, 5% is safer.
[00:04:25] Priya: Ok. How long do we hold at each step? 15 min, 30 min?
[00:04:29] Daniel: 30 minutes for initial hold — enough to see tail behavior — then double hold after 20% increments. We can make the timing conditional in the runbook.

[00:05:00] Priya: Alerts — we need to make sure our on-call doesn't get paged for noise. What thresholds should map to pages versus tickets?
[00:05:07] Sofia: (laugh) small typo earlier — but good question. We usually recommend paging for sustained p99 breaches > 2x SLO for 15 minutes or error rate above 0.5% for two consecutive windows. Non-urgent anomalies go to a ticket. We'll send a suggested mapping.
[00:05:25] Ethan: Can you give concrete numbers? Our SLO is 200ms p99 so paging threshold would be 400ms p99 sustained, correct?
[00:05:31] Daniel: Yes, that's a good starting point. Also page on request timeouts or elevated 5xxs above 0.5% for 10 minutes.

[00:06:25] Sofia: Criteria — we have automatic traffic switchback and manual failover option. Automatic rollback will default to the last known-good model variant and hold traffic at control. Manual rollback requires operator confirmation after which we re-run the pre-warm.
[00:06:45] Ethan: Who has permission to initiate rollback? We need RBAC in console so not anyone can flip traffic.
[00:06:52] Lena: Good point — we'll add RBAC steps in the runbook; by default only Ops and Platform leads have rollback rights.

[00:07:20] Daniel: On observability — we created a dashboard template in the Console: per-route p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput, rerank quality proxy, and infra signals (GPU memory, queue length). We'll share the dashboard link.
[00:07:35] Priya: Please include a panel for model variant comparison so we can see control vs canary side-by-side.
[00:07:39] Daniel: Yes, side-by-side and delta panels. Also we'll wire a synthetic probe hitting the canary route every minute hitting your top-intent set.

[00:08:10] Tom: Regarding network and data residency — we need to ensure request logs are sent to our SIEM and that logs do not include PII. Are the audit logs persisted and filterable?
[00:08:20] Sofia: For Private and Dedicated we support routing logs to your SIEM and we can redact or hash PII fields; we'll share the security guide and our SOC 2 summary.
[00:08:33] Marisol: Can we keep verbose debug logs only in staging, not prod?
[00:08:36] Daniel: Yes, debug logging can be gated by a flag and exported only to staging buckets; prod will keep structured traces and metrics.

[00:09:05] Priya: One more on A/B: We want to run a feature A/B that surfaces a new prompt template and measure engagement and error uplift. Does Redwood support per-customer routing or only per-route?
[00:09:16] Sofia: You can do both. The routing layer supports cookie and header based weighting; we can pin by user id for long-running experiments.

[00:09:42] Ethan: For the dry-run on staging — what validation tests should we run? We want checklist items.
[00:09:49] Daniel: Suggested checklist: 1) Pre-warm KV cache synthetic; 2) Run 1 hour soak at 50% QPS; 3) Validate regression test set; 4) Confirm telemetry dashboards ingesting; 5) Verify rollback and RBAC; 6) Confirm SIEM log delivery. We'll put this in the runbook as discrete steps.

[00:10:20] Marisol: Time wise — we said dry-run on 2025-09-10 earlier, is that still good?
[00:10:24] Priya: Yes, team is ok with that but need runbook by 09-05.

[00:10:45] Sofia: On communications — during cutover you should notify product, ops, and support channels; we recommend a brief status bot in your #deployments slack channel and an incident channel standing by.
[00:10:58] Tom: We'll do that. Who will own the post-cutover smoke test?
[00:11:02] Ethan: Ops will own smoke test and then hand to Product for functional checks.

[00:11:25] Daniel: A small note on caching and batching to save cost during canary: enable adaptive batching but with max latency cap, Redwood Optimize suggested these settings — the idea is to trade micro-latency for fewer tokens charged. We'll surface recommended batch size and quantization profile in the runbook.
[00:11:48] Marisol: Quantization profile — does that change quality? We can't have user-visible regressions.
[00:11:52] Daniel: If you're using mild int8 quantization (our recommended profile for this model), quality diff is negligible on your eval set; we'll include eval deltas in the runbook.

[00:12:30] Priya: Anything else from Redwood before we close?
[00:12:34] Daniel: I'll summarize the proposed canary plan in bullets: start 5% canary -> hold 30m -> check p50/p95/p99/error/quality -> ramp to 20% -> hold 60m -> ramp to 50% -> full cutover if stable. Auto-rollback on guard fail.
[00:12:50] Sofia: And I'll attach the runbook + rollback checklist and the dry-run checklist. Also sending the dashboard link and a small script for pre-warm.
[00:13:10] Priya: Great. Quick question — what's the expected impact on cost during canary? We want a high-level estimate.
[00:13:18] Sofia: With 5% traffic routed to the canary, cost bump is near-linear for token usage — so roughly 5% plus overhead for parallelism/extra probes. We'll include an estimated delta in the runbook; Redwood Optimize recommendations can further reduce it.
[00:13:42] Ethan: For SLA — when we shift to Dedicated later, will SLA change?
[00:13:48] Sofia: Dedicated comes with committed capacity and SLA guarantees; we'll discuss contract language with sales and legal after the pilot. For now pilot is in hosted sandbox.
[00:14:20] Priya: One operational wrinkle — our legal wants a short note on log retention and deletion policy for PII.
[00:14:26] Sofia: We'll include the data retention addendum and options for log redaction.
[00:14:50] Marisol: Ok, let's recap.
[00:14:53] Sofia: Recap: 1) Sofia sends cutover runbook + rollback checklist (due 09-05); 2) Daniel sends telemetry/log exports and dashboard link (due 09-04); 3) KiteWave to confirm canary percentages and SLO owners (due 09-06); 4) Dry-run scheduled 09-10 staging; 5) Ethan runs kv-cache soak test and posts results (due 09-08).
[00:15:20] Priya: That matches our notes. Any blockers?
[00:15:24] Tom: RBAC change in console — need confirmation that only Ops can rollback. We'll need a short doc on how to set that up.
[00:15:31] Lena: We'll add RBAC steps to the runbook and a how-to doc.
[00:15:50] Sofia: OK. I'll open a shared drive folder and drop the runbook and scripts; Daniel will drop telemetry artifacts. We'll link the CRM deal with the dry-run milestone.
[00:16:05] Marisol: One last note — product would like a light A/B analytics snippet so we can compare engagement metrics across variants. Is that part of the dashboard?
[00:16:15] Daniel: Yes, we'll add engagement KPIs as part of the variant comparison panels.
[00:16:40] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with materials and confirm dry-run time in the calendar.
[00:16:48] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:16:50] Ethan: Thanks.

[00:20:00] (Call continues with smaller technical clarifications and off-line sequencing; meeting ends at 14:54)

Post-call notes: runbook link placeholder: https://drive.redwood.example/runbooks/kitewave-cutover-2025-09-03 (will be finalized by 09-05). Dashboard placeholder: https://console.redwood.example/dashboards/kw-poc-canary

Errors/odd transcriptions: occasional substitution of "kv-cache" as "K V cash", Redwood product names spaced out by ASR (Red wood D e d i c a t e d), and minor speaker attribution glitches.
